quizzes.title: Wetlands and Their Forms: MCQ
quizzes.passage: A wetland is a place in which the land is covered by water. That water may be salt, fresh or somewhere in between. Wetlands take many forms, so the term covers a wide range of landscapes. Lakes and rivers are among the most familiar of them, and swamps and wet grasslands also count as wetlands. Along the coast, mangroves are one of the forms the booklet describes, and coral reefs and other coastal areas appear in the same list. Marshes and bogs are also listed among the forms of wetlands. Some forms sit inland, while others lie near the sea. Wet grasslands and peatlands show that the water need not always form a lake. The booklet's list of water bodies is long, and it reaches from freshwater lakes to sea-edge habitats. The common feature in the definition is that land is covered by water, rather than any single shape or size. This is why a wetland can be a large lake, a river, a swamp or a stretch of grassland. The definition therefore allows a broad range of habitats to be counted within one category. Each of these forms is still a place where the land is covered by water. The booklet presents these forms as examples of a single category, which is the wetland.

questions.q: How many segments are wetlands classified into?
questions.explanation: The booklet classifies wetlands into three segments: inland, coastal and human-made wetlands.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the segments into which wetlands are classified?
questions.explanation: Human-made wetlands is one of the three segments named in the booklet.

questions.q: Which of these is named among the other forms of wetlands in the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet's list of other forms ends with floodplains, after lagoons and lakes.

questions.q: Which of these is listed alongside peatlands and wet grasslands in the booklet's list of water bodies?
questions.explanation: The booklet's list of water bodies includes deltas, next to wet grasslands and peatlands.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Wetlands can be covered by water for part of the year.
Reason (R): The water cover of a wetland may be seasonal.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A seasonal water cover is the reason a wetland can be covered by water for only part of the year.

questions.q:
I. Tidal flats are named among the forms of wetland in the booklet.
II. Human-made wetlands is one of the three segments of wetlands.
III. Ponds are classified as a segment of wetlands.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Tidal flats are in the booklet's list of forms and human-made wetlands is a segment, while ponds are a form and not a segment.

questions.q:
I. Mudflats are named among the forms of wetlands.
II. Ponds are named among the forms of wetlands.
III. Wetlands are classified into four segments.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Mudflats and ponds are both named as forms, while the booklet gives three segments and not four.

questions.q: Name the wetland segment that is neither inland nor coastal.
questions.explanation: The three segments are inland, coastal and human-made wetlands.

questions.q: Name the wetland form that the booklet lists last among its other forms (one word).
questions.explanation: The booklet's list of other forms ends with lakes and floodplains.

questions.q: Name the underground water body that the booklet lists among wetlands (one word).
questions.explanation: The booklet lists underground aquifers among the water bodies that count as wetlands.

questions.q: In the booklet's list of water bodies, which form comes immediately after 'Deltas' (two words)?
questions.explanation: The list reads deltas, tidal flats, mangroves, coral reefs and other coastal areas.

questions.q: In the booklet's list of other forms, which form comes immediately after 'mudflats' (one word)?
questions.explanation: The list reads mangroves, mudflats, ponds, swamps, billabongs, lagoons, lakes and floodplains.

questions.q: In the booklet's list of other forms, which form comes immediately after 'swamps' (one word)?
questions.explanation: The list reads ponds, swamps, billabongs, lagoons, lakes and floodplains.

quizzes.title: Ramsar Convention in Brief: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Ramsar Convention is an intergovernmental treaty that concerns wetlands. It is a formal agreement among its member countries, and it has 172 member states. The treaty focuses on wetlands of international importance. India is one of the countries that take part in the treaty. World Wetlands Day is observed every year to draw attention to wetlands and their value. Each year's observance carries a theme. The treaty takes its name from the Iranian city of Ramsar, where it was signed. The Montreux Record is a register of wetland sites. It records sites where changes in ecological character have occurred or are likely to occur. Such changes may result from technological developments, pollution or other human interference. Indian wetlands have appeared in the record. The Montreux Record is one of the tools linked to the treaty's work. Wetlands are areas of land covered by water, which may be salt, fresh or in between. The booklet describes wetlands as places with many water bodies, such as lakes, rivers and swamps. Wetlands are associated in the booklet with biodiversity and carbon stock. The booklet also notes that the treaty and World Wetlands Day share a focus on wetlands. Wetland conservation is therefore a shared concern for the countries in the treaty.

questions.q: What is the theme of World Wetlands Day 2026?
options: Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage
questions.explanation: The 2026 theme of World Wetlands Day is Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage.

questions.q: How often does the Conference of Parties (COP) to the Ramsar Convention meet?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Conference of Parties meets every 3 years.

questions.q: What is the official name of the Ramsar Convention?
options: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
questions.explanation: The official name of the Ramsar Convention is the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Wetlands of international importance are declared as Ramsar sites.
Reason (R): The Ramsar Convention is the only international treaty that addresses a specific ecosystem.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the fact that the Convention addresses one ecosystem does not explain how sites are declared.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Montreux Record was launched in   ->   A. 1975
II. Ramsar Convention came into force in   ->   B. 2 February
III. India became a signatory in   ->   C. 1990
IV. World Wetlands Day is observed on   ->   D. 1982
questions.explanation: The Montreux Record was launched in 1990, the Convention came into force in 1975, India became a signatory in 1982 and World Wetlands Day is on 2 February.

questions.q:
I. COP14 of the Ramsar Convention was co-held in 2022 in Wuhan (China) and Geneva (Switzerland).
II. The Montreux Record identifies Ramsar sites that need priority conservation attention.
III. World Wetlands Day is celebrated on 22 March.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while World Wetlands Day is celebrated on 2 February, not 22 March.

questions.q:
I. The Convention was adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran.
II. The Conference of Parties meets every 2 years.
III. The Ramsar Convention has been in force since 1971.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only the adoption statement is correct, since the Convention came into force in 1975 and COP meets every 3 years.

questions.q: In which year did the Ramsar Convention come into force? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Convention came into force in 1975.

questions.q: In which year did India become a signatory to the Ramsar Convention? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India became a signatory on 1 February 1982.

questions.q: On which date (day and month) is World Wetlands Day celebrated?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that World Wetlands Day is celebrated on 2 February.

questions.q: In which year was the Montreux Record launched? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Montreux Record was launched in 1990.

questions.q: In the 2026 World Wetlands Day theme, which two words follow 'Celebrating'?
questions.explanation: The 2026 theme is Wetlands and Traditional Knowledge: Celebrating Cultural Heritage.

questions.q: In which Chinese city was COP14 of the Ramsar Convention co-held in 2022? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that COP14 was co-held in 2022 in Wuhan (China) and Geneva.

questions.q: In which Swiss city was COP14 of the Ramsar Convention co-held in 2022? (city)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that COP14 was co-held in 2022 in Wuhan (China) and Geneva (Switzerland).
